title: Beef, ground, 90% lean meat / 10% fat, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Ground beef with 90% lean meat and 10% fat is raw meat obtained by grinding beef. It has a rich meaty flavor, a tender texture, and is used in a wide range of dishes, from patties to sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ground beef is a staple in many cuisines, such as American burgers and Italian ragù.
The 10% fat content makes it leaner than typical 15‑20% ground beef while retaining juiciness.
Ground beef can be frozen for up to 6 months without quality loss if stored in airtight packaging.
Proper grinding preserves most of the meat’s nutrients, including iron and vitamin B12.
Ground beef is often used as a base for making sausages and meatballs.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Ground beef provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is a great source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed and supports healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is important for red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Ground beef contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Raw beef may harbor pathogenic bacteria such as E. coli or Salmonella. Cook to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Even at 10% fat, the meat contains saturated fats, which should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: Cholesterol
items.content: Ground beef contains cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor portion sizes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ground beef can be sautéed, braised, baked, or used as a filling for pies, burgers, meatballs, and sauces. Thaw in the refrigerator before cooking and break up clumps for even cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw ground beef in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container for up to 6 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
